notes: No primary quote positively stating FORTRAN's influence on ALGOL 58/60 could be verified in this session: the ACM Digital Library returned 403, the open copies of the HOPL papers are image scans the fetch tool cannot read, and PDF page rendering is not available locally. What was readable points the other way or is secondary: de Beer's 'The History of ALGOL' (https://heerdebeer.org/ALGOL/creation.html, secondary) says the American subcommittee chose 'to ignore the existence of FORTRAN' because of IBM's dominance, while noting that Backus 'also participated in the creation of IAL at the Zürich meeting'; the Software Preservation Group's ALGOL page quotes the Bauer and Samelson ICIP 1959 abstract, 'There was no question that the language like FORTRAN should be an operational constructive language' (truncated; a European primary source naming FORTRAN as a model for the kind of language, worth reading in full: paper/Bauer_Samelson-ICIP-1959.pdf on that site). Suggested next step: read the Perlis HOPL paper as a PDF by hand (or with OCR) and search for 'FORTRAN'; also the Bauer and Samelson 1959 paper. Until then the tie stays contested, and the only primary-sourced positive fact is organizational (Backus, FORTRAN's lead designer, was one of the four ACM delegates at Zurich), which by the brief's rule would make it weak.
